iconicAnchor.label: Hungarian regional folk embroidery
iconicAnchor.whyCanonical: The Smithsonian account ties visible technique, base material, yarn, motif change, and named regional variation together, making it a useful anchor for tradition-specific rather than generic embroidery.

sources.title: Folk Embroidery
supports: Embroidery styles vary with base material, yarn, stitch, motif, and named regional practice.

sources.title: Embroidered Pictures
supports: Embroidery uses needle and thread on cloth and can form pictorial, historical, devotional, and domestic subjects through distinct materials and techniques.

bundledReferenceRationale: Excellent single-image set. The lead clearly teaches visible thread, named regional motifs, stitch density, cloth ground, retains its identity at card scale, and shows no visible anti-cue, integrity failure, or confusing overlap with neighboring styles. The independently approved lead is assets/refs/folk-embroidery/reference-01.jpg. No support image is needed because the lead carries the direction without filler.

culturalContext.note: Treat folk embroidery as many living and historical practices, not a universal decorative vocabulary. Name the community and region, distinguish ceremonial or identity-bearing motifs from general stitch structure, retain maker attribution where known, and avoid combining symbols from unrelated traditions into a placeless ethnic pattern.
